newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia state-owned Telstra posts record profit.
newsitem.headline: Australia state-owned Telstra posts record profit.

text.p: Australian state-owned telecommunications carrier Telstra Corp on Friday rang up a record profit of A$2.3 billion (US$1.8 billion), but immediately announced it would shed almost a third of its staff.

Telstra's profit after tax and abnormals jumped 31.5 percent in the year to June 30 to surpass the National Australia Bank as corporate Australia's biggest earner, and the carrier declared a windfall dividend to the government of about A$1.4 billion.

But the announcement comes as Telstra finds itself at the centre of a political storm over the conservative government's plan to sell a third of the company, once widely considered to be a "sacred cow" of Australia's state assets.
In preparation for its part privatisation, Telstra announced on Friday it would cut its staff of roughly 76,000 by 22,000 over the next three fiscal years.

Telstra has already said it will cut 9,000 jobs in 1996/97 and announced on Friday it would slash another 13,000 jobs in the following two years. In 1996/97 alone, it has set aside A$1.1 billion to pay for the redundancy programme.

The announcement follows suggestions from stock market analysts that Telstra needs to lay off roughly a third of its staff to boost efficiency to international benchmarks and guarantee the best return to the government from privatisation.

"It is critical that the corporation continues to make efficiency gains and, indeed, accelerates these gains, if we are to compete effectively with our global and domestic competitors," Telstra chief executive Frank Blount said in a statement.

The government's plan to raise an estimated A$8 billion from the part-sale faces an uncertain future in the upper House of parliament, where a few independent and Green senators may effectively have the casting vote on the sale legislation.
